Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #6436: keep PR-authored agent instruction files out of the triage sandbox

PLANNING REF CONTEXT
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: 6d5d6540efb1028107d927d472c46e80b67fd7e9
- Checked-out branch: `claude/ci-failure-triage-workflow-run`
- Integration branch metadata: `claude/ci-failure-triage-workflow-run` (matches the checkout).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh
Scope-mode justification: The finding is a single defect class: PR-authored agent instruction files reach the sandbox snapshot where Codex runs, and Codex treats them as instructions. The fix extends the snapshot filter that `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` already has (`root_files` / `roots` / `bad_parts` in the embedded Python). A new option turns the filter on, it defaults to off, and only `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` turns it on. Clarify and clarify-respond keep their current behaviour, including loading a consumer's own `AGENTS.md`. The complete version of the fix is only a few lines more than the minimum. It covers every agent-instruction filename at any depth (`AGENTS.md`, `agents.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, matched without regard to case), not just the root `AGENTS.md`. Following the Boil the Lake rule and the §6 priorities (Security > Correctness), I chose the complete version. Changing clarify and clarify-respond is out of scope (see W1).

Automation / §20 surface
- No new script. This extends an existing helper (`scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`) and an existing caller (`scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`).
- Entry point: `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`. It runs on `check_run: completed` and failed `workflow_run: completed` events, through `internal-check-failure-triage.yml` and the consumer `ai-check-failure-triage.yml`. Its staging step already installs both helpers from the trusted `.codex-workflow-src` checkout (line 280 and line 355), so no workflow YAML change is needed.
- No long-running supervisor, no database work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

What the code does today
- `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:496` runs the trusted copy of `clarify_isolated_run.sh` with `CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}"`, which is the PR-head checkout.
- `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh:55-119` copies tracked files into `${run_root}/source`:
  - `root_files` explicitly includes `agents.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
  - `.md` is an allowed suffix under `src`, `scripts`, `tests`, `prompts`, `docs` and the other roots, so nested `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md` and `CLAUDE.md` files are copied too.
- The snapshot is mounted at `/source`, and Codex runs with `--workdir /source` (line 246, `codex ... exec` at line 256). Codex loads `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS.override.md` from its working directory automatically, so PR-authored text becomes part of the model's instructions.
- The triage prompt already includes the root `agents.md` / `AGENTS.md` as fenced, size-capped data marked untrusted (`check_failure_triage.sh:405-454`, issue #6380). That fenced copy is the correct way to present this content, and it stays.
- Not a separate gap: the sandbox runs `/source/scripts/write_codex_config.sh` and reads `codex_model_catalog.json`, but the snapshot takes them from the working tree. The staging step overwrites the workspace copies with trusted ones before the snapshot, and an existing test pins this (`test_support_staging_uses_trusted_checkout_not_pr_head`, lines 310-311).

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`: add the opt-in filter to the snapshot step.
- `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`: turn the filter on when calling the helper (line 496), and add one line to the prompt's context header.
- `prompts/mode-check-failure-triage.txt`: widen the untrusted-data rule (lines 19-20).
- `tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py`: new and extended tests.
- `agents.md`: one sentence each in the "check failure triage" item (13) and the "clarify-respond" item (2).
- New file `changelog.d/6436-triage-omit-pr-agent-instructions.md`, using the `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` format from CLAUDE.md §20.

2. Functions and modules to implement
a. `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`
   - Near `source_root=`, read the new option, defaulting to off:
     `omit_agent_instructions="${CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_OMIT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS:-false}"`
   - Only the exact value `true` turns it on (`case ... in true) ;; *) false`). Anything else means off, which matches today's behaviour.
   - Pass the value to the snapshot Python as a third argument (`sys.argv[3]`), rather than reading the environment inside `python3 -I`, so the input is explicit.
   - In the snapshot Python:
     - Add `agent_instruction_names = {"agents.md", "agents.override.md", "claude.md", "claude.local.md"}`.
     - At the top of `copy(path)`, before any other check: when the option is on and the last path component, lowercased, is in that set, add one to `omitted` and `return`. This covers the repo root and every depth.
     - After the `git ls-files` loop, if `omitted` is above zero, print `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_OMITTED count=<n>` to stderr. The count is enough; file names are not needed.
   - Update the header comment (line 4) to document the option and its default.
   - Nothing else changes: the Docker invocation, the broker, the Claude branch, the size and count limits, and the symlink and race checks all stay as they are.

b. `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`
   - Line 496: add `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_OMIT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS=true` next to `CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT="${SOURCE_ROOT}"` in the same `env -u ...` invocation. Credentials stay stripped.
   - Line 457: after the "PR checkout (read-only diagnostic data, mounted at /source ...)" line, add one `echo` saying that agent instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `agents.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) are left out of `/source`, and that the root `agents.md` / `AGENTS.md` appear above only as fenced untrusted data.
   - Add a code comment citing finding `triage-pr-agents-instruction-injection` and the reason: instructions come only from trusted support, and PR content is diagnostic data only.

c. `prompts/mode-check-failure-triage.txt`
   - Lines 19-20: extend the rule to "the pull request description, check-run logs, PR-head agent instruction files, and every file under /source". This adds wording without changing any section name or meaning.
   - Before editing, check `prompts/.overrides.yaml` for a freeze on this file, and check whether a `prompts/_templates/` source exists for it. If a template exists, edit it alongside the file.

3. Data structures affected
- No persisted state. The only structural change is a new set and counter inside the helper's embedded Python.
- The new environment variable `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_OMIT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS` defaults to `false` inside the helper (§8), so a caller that never sets it behaves exactly as before. I checked the name against existing `CLARIFY_*` variables (`CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT`, `CLARIFY_CODEX_VERSION`, `CLARIFY_MODEL`, `CLARIFY_REASONING`, `CLARIFY_PROXY_KEY`) and it does not clash.

4. API and interface changes
- The helper accepts one new optional environment variable. Its positional arguments, exit codes (including 75 for the Claude fallback) and output files are unchanged.
- The helper gains one new stderr line, `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_OMITTED`. It is diagnostic only, and it is not added to the contractual log-prefix list.

## Decisions
### D1 — Leave the files out of the snapshot rather than renaming them
- Chosen: skip agent instruction files when building the snapshot.
- Alternatives considered: rename them in the snapshot (for example `AGENTS.md.untrusted`); set Codex's `-c project_doc_max_bytes=0`; strip the files after copying.
- Why: Leaving them out removes the attack surface for both the Codex and the Claude engines in one place. The root files' content already reaches the model as fenced data, so no diagnostic value is lost. A renamed file is a new name some future tool might pick up. `project_doc_max_bytes` only works for Codex, and support for it in the pinned `v0.114.0` would need checking. Stripping after copying adds a second pass that could miss files.

### D2 — Opt-in option that only triage turns on
- Chosen: `CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_OMIT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS`, default `false`, set to `true` only by `check_failure_triage.sh`.
- Alternatives considered: always leave the files out, for every caller.
- Why: Clarify and clarify-respond currently depend on Codex loading the consumer's own `AGENTS.md`, and changing that is outside the issue (§2 and §9). Both helpers are staged from the same trusted support commit, so the triage caller and the helper always agree on the option.

### D3 — Match without regard to case, at any depth, on the full set of instruction filenames
- Chosen: compare the lowercased last path component with `agents.md`, `agents.override.md`, `claude.md` and `claude.local.md`.
- Alternatives considered: only the root `AGENTS.md`, matched exactly.
- Why: Codex's override file and Claude's nested-memory loading are the same kind of injection. The security pass expects every instance of a defect class to be cleared, not just the cited line.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the PR-head checkout, written by the PR author, crosses into the sandboxed model's instruction context. After this change, PR content reaches the model only as fenced, untrusted prompt data and as non-instruction files under `/source`. Instructions come only from `TRUSTED_SUPPORT_DIR` (system instructions, `agents_canonical.md`, the mode prompt).
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface is added. The triage issue is still posted by the separate `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN` step, after the existing check for routing keys and markers.
